chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) met Abdullah ibn Ja'far, so he said: 'O Abdullah! How can the believer be a believer while he is angry at his portion (divine decree) and belittles his status, with Allah being the Ruler over him? And I am the guarantor that whoever does not have in his heart except satisfaction, that if he supplicates to Allah, He will answer him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the connection between contentment with divine decree and the acceptance of supplication in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) defines true faith (*Iman*) as inseparable from inner contentment (*Rida*) with Allah’s decree, warning that dissatisfaction reveals a deficiency in belief. He further establishes a spiritual guarantee that those whose hearts are free from grumbling will have their supplications answered, a concept deeply rooted in Shia theology regarding the connection between divine will and human acceptance.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws met Abdullah Bin Ja’far, so heasws said: ‘O Abdullah! How can the Momin happen to be a Momin and he is angry at his distribution, and he belittles his status, and the Ruler upon him is Allahazwj? And Iasws am the guarantor to the one who does not have a notion in his heart except for the satisfaction that he would supplicate to Allahazwj, so Heazwj would Answer to him’.
en.sarwar: 11. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn Ali from Ali ibn Asbat from those whom he has mentioned from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Al-Hassan ibn Ali (a.s.) once met ‘Abd Allah ibn Ja’far and said to him, ‘O, ‘Abd Allah, how can a believer be a believer when he disagrees with the decision of Allah about his share and belittles his position while the nder over him is Allah? I guarantee that Allah accepts the prayer of one in whose heart (mind) no suggestion takes place except agreement with the decisions of Allah).’”
